newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia coal strike prospect stronger - union.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia coal strike prospect stronger - union.

text.p: Australia's Construction, Forestry Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU) was pursuing initiatives in a bid to avert a national coal strike, general president John Maitland said on Wednesday.

These included an investigation of whether the union could dispose of assets in a colliery where 137 miners have been retrenched, or find a joint-venture partner willing to operate the mine, he told Reuters.

But statements by the colliery's official administrator Price Waterhouse on Tuesday night that only A$700,000 was presently available to settle full retrenchment and severance entitlements of A$4.9 million for the sacked miners strengthened the prospect of the strike going ahead, he said.
"We have three weeks to sort this out," Maitland said.
The CFMEU has set a December 11 deadline for full payment of the entitlements if a national coal strike is to be averted.

Price Waterhouse administrator Nick Brooke told Reuters on Tuesday that the only way sacked workers could be paid more than the A$700,000 now available would be if owners of the colliery agreed to pay the former employees from proceeds of a mine sale. The mine involved, Metropolitan Collieries Ltd, south of Sydney, is owned 90 percent by Australia's Denehurst Ltd and 10 percent by Japan's Kanematsu Corp.
Both companies are also fixed-charged creditors, with Kanematsu ranking as first secured creditor for A$20 million.

The CFMEU would hold a meeting on Friday with the Maritime Union of Australia, which staged a stopwork at Australia's four biggest ports on Tuesday night to protest passage of industrial relations legislation through the Australian Senate, Maitland said.
Union opposition to the industrial relations legislation made a national coal strike a possibility regardless of developments at Metropolitan Collieries, he said.
The CFMEU announced on Tuesday that it would sanction a national coal strike unless the retrenched employees received their full severance and retrenchment entitlements.
Coal exports, Australia's biggest commodity trade, are forecast to reach almost 150 million tonnes worth about A$8.2 billion in 1996/97.
Most of the coal goes to Asia, with Japanese steel mills and power stations the biggest customers.
